ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in square $ABCD$, circle $O$ with diameter $AB$ intersects the midpoint of side $BC$ at point $E$ and intersects diagonal $AC$ at point $F$. Draw $EG \perp AC$ with the foot of the perpendicular at $M$. If $FA=3CF$, what is the value of $\frac{CG}{GD}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect BF and extend GE, where AB intersects at point H, let AC intersect GE at point M,\\
since AB is the diameter of circle O,\\
therefore $\angle AFB=90^\circ$,\\
since quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram,\\
therefore $DC\parallel AB$, $DC=AB$,\\
therefore $\angle DCE=\angle CBH$, $\angle CGE=\angle EHB$,\\
since E is the midpoint of BC,\\
therefore $CE=BE=\frac{1}{2}CB$,\\
therefore $\triangle GEC\cong \triangle HEB$ (AAS),\\
therefore $GC=BH$,\\
since $EG\perp AC$, $BF\perp AC$,\\
therefore $ME\parallel BF$,\\
therefore $CM:CF=CE:CB=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
therefore let $CM=MF=a$, $CF=2a$,\\
therefore $FA=3CF=6a$,\\
therefore $CM:MA=a:7a=\frac{1}{7}$,\\
since $CD\parallel AB$\\
therefore $\triangle GMC\sim \triangle HMA$,\\
therefore $GC:AH=MC:MA=\frac{1}{7}$,\\
therefore $GC:AB=\frac{1}{6}$,\\
therefore $GC:CD=\frac{1}{6}$,\\
therefore $GC:DG=\boxed{\frac{1}{5}}$.

method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一个标有 A、B、C、D 的正方形或平行四边形形状，AB 为下边，CD 为上边，BC 在右侧。以 AB 为直径画有圆 O，圆与右边 BC 交于点 E，E 位于 BC 中点附近；圆还与对角线 AC 交于点 F。过 E 作一条斜线与 AC 垂直，这条线向上交 CD 于 G，向下延长会交 AB 的延长线于 H；它与 AC 的交点是 M。图中点的顺序与方法草案一致：G 在 CD 上，E 在 BC 上，F、M 在 AC 上。

推理：连接 BF，并延长 GE 交 AB 的延长线于 H。因为 AB 是圆 O 的直径，F 在圆上，所以由泰勒斯定理得 ∠AFB = 90°，即 BF ⟂ AC。又因为题设 EG ⟂ AC，且 M 在 EG 与 AC 的交点上，所以 ME ∥ BF。

在三角形 CBF 中，E 是 CB 的中点，过 E 作平行于 BF 的直线交 CF 于 M，因此由中位线定理，M 是 CF 的中点，所以 CM:CF = 1:2。设 CM = MF = a，则 CF = 2a。已知 FA = 3CF，所以 FA = 6a，因此 MA = MF + FA = a + 6a = 7a。于是 CM:MA = a:7a = 1:7。

因为 CD ∥ AB，且 G、M、H 共线，C、M、A 共线，所以三角形 GMC 与三角形 HMA 相似。因此 GC:AH = MC:MA = 1:7，即 AH = 7GC。

再看三角形 GEC 与 HEB。由于 CD ∥ AB，所以 GC ∥ HB；又 G、E、H 共线，C、E、B 共线。于是 ∠DCE 与 ∠CBH 对应，∠CGE 与 ∠EHB 对应；并且 E 是 BC 的中点，所以 CE = BE。因此三角形 GEC 与 HEB 可由 AAS 判定全等，从而 GC = BH。

因为 H 在 B 的外侧，所以 AH = AB + BH。代入 AH = 7GC 且 BH = GC，得到 AB = AH - BH = 7GC - GC = 6GC。正方形中 CD = AB，所以 CD = 6GC。又 G 在 CD 上，故 GD = CD - CG = 6CG - CG = 5CG。因此 CG/GD = 1/5。

推理：连接 BF，并延长 GE 交 AB 的延长线于 H。因为 AB 是圆 O 的直径，F 在圆上，所以由泰勒斯定理得 ∠AFB = 90°，即 BF ⟂ AC。又因为题设 EG ⟂ AC，且 M 在 EG 与 AC 的交点上，所以 ME ∥ BF。

在三角形 CBF 中，E 是 CB 的中点，过 E 作平行于 BF 的直线交 CF 于 M，因此由中位线定理，M 是 CF 的中点，所以 CM:CF = 1:2。设 CM = MF = a，则 CF = 2a。已知 FA = 3CF，所以 FA = 6a，因此 MA = MF + FA = a + 6a = 7a。于是 CM:MA = a:7a = 1:7。

因为 CD ∥ AB，且 G、M、H 共线，C、M、A 共线，所以三角形 GMC 与三角形 HMA 相似。因此 GC:AH = MC:MA = 1:7，即 AH = 7GC。

再看三角形 GEC 与 HEB。由于 CD ∥ AB，所以 GC ∥ HB；又 G、E、H 共线，C、E、B 共线。于是 ∠DCE 与 ∠CBH 对应，∠CGE 与 ∠EHB 对应；并且 E 是 BC 的中点，所以 CE = BE。因此三角形 GEC 与 HEB 可由 AAS 判定全等，从而 GC = BH。

因为 H 在 B 的外侧，所以 AH = AB + BH。代入 AH = 7GC 且 BH = GC，得到 AB = AH - BH = 7GC - GC = 6GC。正方形中 CD = AB，所以 CD = 6GC。又 G 在 CD 上，故 GD = CD - CG = 6CG - CG = 5CG。因此 CG/GD = 1/5。

图像描述：附图中，AB 是下方一条水平线段，并作为圆 O 的直径；圆经过 A、B，并与斜边 BC 上的点 E 相交。四边形 ABCD 画成上边 CD 与下边 AB 平行的斜四边形，D、G、C 在上边 CD 上，G 位于 D 与 C 之间。对角线 AC 被画出，点 F 在 AC 上且也在圆上；从 E 向上作直线与 CD 交于 G，并与 AC 垂直，垂足记为 M。

推理：按指定方法，用向量建模。取 A 为原点，令 B = u，C = u + v，D = v，因此 CD 平行于 AB。归一化 |u| = 1。由题意 E 是 BC 的中点，所以 E = u + v/2。又 F 在 AC 上且 FA = 3CF，即 AF:FC = 3:1，所以 F = 3(u + v)/4。

圆以 AB 为直径。对任意在该圆上的点 X，有向量条件 X · (X - u) = 0。

先代入 E：E · (E - u) = (u + v/2) · (v/2) = 0，所以 2(u·v) + |v|^2 = 0。

再代入 F：F = 3(u + v)/4，代入 X · (X - u) = 0，化简得 -|u|^2 + 2(u·v) + 3|v|^2 = 0。因为 |u| = 1，所以 -1 + 2(u·v) + 3|v|^2 = 0。

联立 2(u·v) + |v|^2 = 0 与 -1 + 2(u·v) + 3|v|^2 = 0，得到 |v|^2 = 1/2，u·v = -1/4。

设 G 在 CD 上，写作 G = v + t u，其中 t = DG/CD。因此 CG/GD = (1 - t)/t。

由于 EG 垂直 AC，方向向量满足 (G - E) · (u + v) = 0。这里 G - E = v + t u - (u + v/2) = (t - 1)u + v/2。

所以 (t - 1)(1 + u·v) + 1/2(u·v + |v|^2) = 0。代入 u·v = -1/4，|v|^2 = 1/2，得 (t - 1)(3/4) + 1/2(1/4) = 0，即 (3/4)(t - 1) + 1/8 = 0，解得 t = 5/6。

于是 DG/CD = 5/6，CG/CD = 1/6，所以 CG/GD = (1/6)/(5/6) = 1/5。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the diagram, in square $ABCD$, circle $O$ with diameter $AB$ intersects the midpoint of side $BC$ at point $E$ and intersects diagonal $AC$ at point $F$. Draw $EG \perp AC$ with the foot of the perpendicular at $M$. If $FA=3CF$, what is the value of $\frac{CG}{GD}$?
raw_record.answer:
As shown in the figure, connect $BF$ and extend $GE$, where $AB$ intersects at point $H$, let $AC$ intersect $GE$ at point $M$.
Since $AB$ is the diameter of circle $O$, therefore $\angle AFB=90^\circ$.
Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a parallelogram, therefore $DC\parallel AB$, $DC=AB$.
Therefore $\angle DCE=\angle CBH$, $\angle CGE=\angle EHB$.
Since $E$ is the midpoint of $BC$, therefore $CE=BE=\frac{1}{2}CB$.
Therefore $\triangle GEC\cong \triangle HEB$ (AAS), so $GC=BH$.
Since $EG\perp AC$, $BF\perp AC$, therefore $ME\parallel BF$.
Therefore $CM:CF=CE:CB=\frac{1}{2}$.
Let $CM=MF=a$, then $CF=2a$.
Therefore $FA=3CF=6a$.
Therefore $CM:MA=a:7a=\frac{1}{7}$.
Since $CD\parallel AB$, therefore $\triangle GMC\sim \triangle HMA$.
Therefore $GC:AH=MC:MA=\frac{1}{7}$.
Therefore $GC:AB=\frac{1}{6}$, so $GC:CD=\frac{1}{6}$.
Therefore $GC:DG=\boxed{\frac{1}{5}}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The figure is a square or parallelogram shape labeled A, B, C, D, with AB as the lower side, CD as the upper side, and BC on the right side. A circle O is drawn with AB as diameter; the circle intersects the right side BC at point E, and E is near the midpoint of BC; the circle also intersects diagonal AC at point F. Through E, draw an oblique line perpendicular to AC; this line intersects CD upward at G, and if extended downward, it will intersect the extension of AB at H; its intersection point with AC is M. The order of the points in the figure is consistent with the draft method: G is on CD, E is on BC, and F and M are on AC.

Reasoning: Connect BF, and extend GE to intersect the extension of AB at H. Because AB is the diameter of circle O and F is on the circle, by Thales' theorem, ∠AFB = 90°, that is, BF ⟂ AC. Also because the given condition is EG ⟂ AC, and M is on the intersection point of EG and AC, ME ∥ BF.

In triangle CBF, E is the midpoint of CB, and the line through E parallel to BF intersects CF at M; therefore by the midline theorem, M is the midpoint of CF, so CM:CF = 1:2. Let CM = MF = a, then CF = 2a. Given FA = 3CF, so FA = 6a, therefore MA = MF + FA = a + 6a = 7a. Thus CM:MA = a:7a = 1:7.

Because CD ∥ AB, and G, M, H are collinear, C, M, A are collinear, triangles GMC and HMA are similar. Therefore GC:AH = MC:MA = 1:7, that is, AH = 7GC.

Now look at triangles GEC and HEB. Since CD ∥ AB, GC ∥ HB; also G, E, H are collinear, and C, E, B are collinear. Thus ∠DCE and ∠CBH correspond, and ∠CGE and ∠EHB correspond; moreover E is the midpoint of BC, so CE = BE. Therefore triangles GEC and HEB can be determined congruent by AAS, hence GC = BH.

Because H is on the outside of B, AH = AB + BH. Substitute AH = 7GC and BH = GC to get AB = AH - BH = 7GC - GC = 6GC. In the square, CD = AB, so CD = 6GC. Also G is on CD, so GD = CD - CG = 6CG - CG = 5CG. Therefore CG/GD = 1/5.

Since $EG\perp AC$, $BF\perp AC$, therefore $ME\parallel BF$. Therefore $CM:CF=CE:CB=\frac{1}{2}$. Let $CM=MF=a$, then $CF=2a$. Therefore $FA=3CF=6a$. Therefore $CM:MA=a:7a=\frac{1}{7}$. Since $CD\parallel AB$, therefore $\triangle GMC\sim \triangle HMA$. Therefore $GC:AH=MC:MA=\frac{1}{7}$. Therefore $GC:AB=\frac{1}{6}$, so $GC:CD=\frac{1}{6}$. Therefore $GC:DG=\boxed{\frac{1}{5}}$.

Image description: The figure is a square or parallelogram shape labeled A, B, C, D, with AB as the lower side, CD as the upper side, and BC on the right side. A circle O is drawn with AB as diameter; the circle intersects the right side BC at point E, and E is near the midpoint of BC; the circle also intersects diagonal AC at point F. Through E, draw an oblique line perpendicular to AC; this line intersects CD upward at G, and if extended downward, it will intersect the extension of AB at H; its intersection point with AC is M. The order of the points in the figure is consistent with the draft method: G is on CD, E is on BC, and F and M are on AC.

Reasoning: Connect BF, and extend GE to intersect the extension of AB at H. Because AB is the diameter of circle O and F is on the circle, by Thales' theorem, ∠AFB = 90°, that is, BF ⟂ AC. Also because the given condition is EG ⟂ AC, and M is on the intersection point of EG and AC, ME ∥ BF.

In triangle CBF, E is the midpoint of CB, and the line through E parallel to BF intersects CF at M; therefore by the midline theorem, M is the midpoint of CF, so CM:CF = 1:2. Let CM = MF = a, then CF = 2a. Given FA = 3CF, so FA = 6a, therefore MA = MF + FA = a + 6a = 7a. Thus CM:MA = a:7a = 1:7.

Because CD ∥ AB, and G, M, H are collinear, C, M, A are collinear, triangles GMC and HMA are similar. Therefore GC:AH = MC:MA = 1:7, that is, AH = 7GC.

Now look at triangles GEC and HEB. Since CD ∥ AB, GC ∥ HB; also G, E, H are collinear, and C, E, B are collinear. Thus ∠DCE and ∠CBH correspond, and ∠CGE and ∠EHB correspond; moreover E is the midpoint of BC, so CE = BE. Therefore triangles GEC and HEB can be determined congruent by AAS, hence GC = BH.

Because H is on the outside of B, AH = AB + BH. Substitute AH = 7GC and BH = GC to get AB = AH - BH = 7GC - GC = 6GC. In the square, CD = AB, so CD = 6GC. Also G is on CD, so GD = CD - CG = 6CG - CG = 5CG. Therefore CG/GD = 1/5.
